minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved a new weekly payment plan for a delinquent restaurant, ahead of its liquor license review.
minutes.summary: The commission approved the Q2 FY24 sewer commitment and the prior minutes. It heard a long report on the billing software conversion, which produced incorrect bill histories, and on pump station maintenance. Its main action was approving a revised payment agreement for the "reboot" business, which owes a large sewer balance, and sending a memo to the select board.

votes.motion: Make the Q2 FY24 sewer commitment as presented by the business manager.
Accept the minutes of the 11/13 meeting.

Approve the revised payment plan for the reboot business: weekly payments, future quarterly bills paid in full on the due date, balance paid in full by May 28, 2024, balance moved to the real estate tax bill, written notice to the property owner, payments applied to the sewer lien.

budget_items.what_was_said: The amount billed was stated and put to a vote; errors in Q2 bills will be adjusted on the Q3 commitment.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer for business manager pay
budget_items.what_was_said: A payroll shortfall for the business manager would be covered from the assistant business manager line. It needed approval from town officials, and the commission was told for awareness only.
FY23 ended with a surplus that was moved to retained earnings, and a retained earnings balance was stated.
A rate increase is expected, but capital needs must be understood first; consultants asked to bring a prioritized wish list on January 9.
Quotes for block heater, button and switch repairs seemed to have excessive labor and travel time; revised quotes are being sought. Three block heaters need replacing.

budget_items.topic: Billing software conversion, incorrect bills and delinquency
budget_items.what_was_said: A number of bills out of just over a thousand had incorrect history. Demands are on hold, delinquency can't be stated because receipts may not be posted to the ledger.
The business had not paid a sewer bill since opening and was far behind. A payment was received that day and a new weekly amount was proposed because the original would not cover interest.

transfers.description: From the assistant business manager line item to the business manager line to cover a payroll shortfall

decisions.decision: The Lemonster intermunicipal agreement will go on the January 9 agenda; members send comments to the business manager, who forwards them to the subcommittee.
The chair will send an informational memo to the select board chair about the billing software problems, with help from the business manager. No vote was taken.
A memo will go to the select board as licensing authority with the agreement terms, asking it to consider revocation of the liquor license if the business defaults.
The next meeting is January 9, with the engineering consultant attending to discuss capital needs and the intermunicipal agreement.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to approve a revised weekly payment plan for a restaurant business with an overdue sewer balance, to be paid in full by May 28, 2024.
The plan moves any remaining balance to the real estate tax bill and applies payments to the sewer lien; a memo will go to the select board as licensing authority.
The commission voted to make the Q2 FY24 sewer commitment as presented by the business manager.
The business manager reported that the billing software conversion left a number of bills with incorrect history, with demands on hold and delinquency not yet statable.
The chair will send an informational memo to the select board chair about the billing software problems; no vote was taken.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills are billed through a new software system that produced incorrect bill histories, so a resident's Q2 bill may be adjusted on the Q3 commitment, and the true size of overdue sewer balances cannot yet be stated.

The payment plan shows a mechanism for unpaid sewer charges: a balance can move to the property's real estate tax bill and be secured by a lien, which touches the property owner's tax bill and the licensing review that follows a default.
A rate increase is expected once capital needs are understood, so sewer users may be asked to accept higher rates after the January 9 discussion.
watch_next: January 9 meeting: the engineering consultant is to discuss capital needs, and the Lemonster intermunicipal agreement is on the agenda.
The memo to the select board, which is to set out the payment agreement terms and ask it to consider revocation of the liquor license if the business defaults.
